2026-09-09.headline: Best-executed erg session in the log.
points: Reps 6–9 identical at 1:57.3. Whole set spans 2.4s (1:58.3 → 1:55.9), fastest rep last. No decay anywhere.
1:57.2 avg = 82.7% of PB. Prescribed midpoint was 1:59.9 (80%), so it was run 2.7 s/500m hot — that, plus sore legs and one rice cake, is most of why it felt 8.5/10.
vs Jun 19, same session: 1:57.2 vs 1:58.1, 3411m vs 3386m, r30 vs r29. June needed a 1:53.6 last rep to get there; these first nine were ~1.2 s/500m faster than June's.
2026-09-09.watch: Rate bought the pace. Reps 1–5: 30 spm, 8.50 m/stroke, peak force 138. Reps 6–10: 31.6 spm, 8.11 m/stroke, peak force 129. Identical split, 4.6% less distance per stroke — invisible in the pace column.
2026-09-09.next: Open at 1:58 and hold. Make stroke-rate discipline the target rather than the split: finish the last rep still at 30–31 spm and ~8.4 m/stroke. The pace looks after itself.
2026-09-09.diff: Sep 16 is 10 × 1:30, not 1:20 — each rep runs 10 s longer and rest goes 1:00 → 1:20, so the work-to-rest ratio actually loosens slightly. The band is unchanged at 75–85%, which means the target is still 1:54.9–2:04.9 off the 1:39.9 PB, midpoint 1:59.9. You ran the 1:20s at 1:57.2, which was 1.7 s/500m faster than the quick end.

2026-09-10.title: Strength B — Posterior + pull
2026-09-10.headline: Strong session — and the second day running you took the prescription up.
points: Trap bar: prescribed 195 (70%), you pulled 205 × 5 × 4 — 74.5% of your 275. The card said “RPE cap 7 — hard cap, Wednesday was hard”, and that cap was there because Wednesday's VO₂ was run 2.7 s/500m hot. Two sessions, two overshoots, one day apart.

Weighted pull-up 4 × 5 @ +25 at RIR 2, every set. That clears double progression, so the card will offer +30 next week. Your own note says 27–30 and questions whether 30 holds over four sets — take +27.5 if the gym has the plate.
CMJ best 19.9″ vs 18.0″ on Tuesday: +1.9″, +10.6% in two days. Either genuine rebound or the measurement moved. No baseline is entered, so the readiness gate can't arm and can't tell you which.
2026-09-10.watch: Hip thrust went into the log as “50kg” while every other load is in pounds. The progression engine reads the number and drops the unit, so next week it compares 50 against 110 lb and tells you to hold. Log it in lb (50 kg ≈ 110 lb) or it silently stalls.
2026-09-10.next: Trap bar 195 as written, and let the RPE cap win over the number — under 7 at 195 is the session working, not the session being easy. Pull-up +27.5, which is the one thing that earned a jump. Chest-supported row: hold 75 and build all three sets to 10 before adding, since last week was 10/8/8. Cable lateral 45, not 55 — your own note said 55 only bought 10 reps at RIR 0–1 against a prescription of 15. Hip thrust in pounds. Suitcase carry is tier 3, so swap it for another loaded carry rather than skipping it a second time.
2026-09-10.diff: Sep 17 is the same card almost line for line: trap bar 4 × 5 @ 70% (195 lb), pull-ups 4 × 5 RIR 2, same accessories in the same order. Two things did move. The “Wednesday was hard” rider has come off the trap bar line — that was an explanation for the cap, not a temporary rule, so 70% and RPE 7 still stand. And the chest-supported row and hip thrust drop from tier 2 to tier 3, which makes them swappable and means they no longer progress. Nothing in the prescription goes up this week; the only progression available is the pull-up.

2026-09-11.title: Rowfit — Threshold
2026-09-11.headline: Rate bought the pace. Rep 2 is the one to copy.
points: 2:03.7 → 1:59.4, average 2:02.1 at 192 W, drag 117. Fastest rep last, and reps 2–7 sat inside 0.7 s of each other — the set was flat by design, not by fade.

2:02.1 is 77.8% of PB, a shade over the top of the prescribed 65–77% band. You ran the edge of threshold rather than inside it, which is why the middle felt monotonous and rep 8 still had 205 W in it.
Rep 1: 25 spm, 9.70 m/stroke. Rep 3: 28 spm, 8.77. Three extra strokes a minute bought 1.5 s/500m, and you held 28 for the last six reps — pace held by adding rate and shortening the stroke.
Strap peaked 169 in FITIV, just over VT2 (167), and only at the end. That is exactly where a threshold day should top out.
2026-09-11.watch: Rep 2 is the template: 2:02.5 at 26 spm, 9.42 m/stroke, 190 W — the same watts as reps 3–6 with two fewer strokes a minute. There, length was paying for the pace; after that, rate was. Opening at 26 and defending the length is the harder and more useful version of this session.
2026-09-11.next: 2:12, not 2:03 — I got this wrong the first time I wrote it. Repeating last Friday's pace would put you roughly 7 s/500m over the top of the band on a day that is prescribed as aerobic, and 4:00 reps punish that more than 3:03 reps do. Open at 2:13 and let it settle to 2:12. Hold 26–28 spm: last Friday you climbed from 25 to 28 and the stroke shortened 0.73 m to pay for it, so the test here is whether you can sit at 26–27 for all seven and still finish with something.
2026-09-11.diff: Sep 18 is 7 × 4:00 off 3:00 rest, and the change that matters is not the rep length. The band drops from 65–77% to 65–70%, so the target range is 2:09.9–2:14.9 with a 2:12.4 midpoint — against 2:02.9–2:14.9 last Friday. You rowed the 750s at 2:02.1. That is 7.8 s/500m faster than the quick end of this week's range. This is not the same session with longer reps; it is a materially easier prescription, and the reps are about a minute longer each.

2026-09-12.title: ATHX 90 — test week
2026-09-12.session: ATHX 90 test week (in place of Strength C)
2026-09-12.headline: A real benchmark four weeks out, and the squat is the number that stands out.
points: Strict press 1RM 95, back squat 3RM 195, deadlift 5RM 225 — all inside one 20-minute block at RPE 9–10, after the hang challenge and the broad jumps. Epley puts the squat at a 215 e1RM and the deadlift at 263.

Against what the console actually runs on — squat 230, deadlift 275, press 95 — that is 93%, 96% and 100%. The press went first, fresh, and matched its number exactly. The squat came second and landed furthest from its, which is the odd one out.
Endurance: 2 rounds + 320m into the third run, so 1,320m of running and 1,500m of rowing in 15:00 — about 6:38 per round of 500m run + 750m row.
Metcon: 1 full round plus everything in round 2 except the burpee broad jumps. Roughly 1.8 rounds in 10:00, around 5:30 a round. The clock stopped you at the burpees; that is a position, not a wall.
2026-09-12.watch: The squat. 230 is on file as a true 1RM you have actually lifted, and every tier-1 squat load in this block is a percentage of it — so if the real working number is nearer 215, you have been squatting about 7% heavy all block. One fatigued 3RM in a time cap is not proof, and Sep 8's VBT said the opposite (peak power still climbing on work set 4 at 180×5, roughly RIR 3). Worth a fresh, properly ramped 3RM before touching the number.
2026-09-12.next: Oct 10 is four weeks out, and Oct 3 is a peak-power test Saturday — the week before the race. Say the word if you want the last fortnight shaped around Oct 10 rather than Dec 5; otherwise the block stays as written, which is what you asked for.

2026-09-14.title: Erg Power Series — Horsepower
2026-09-14.headline: 577 W peak at drag 127 — Saturday's number, inside an 88-second piece.
points: Official score 577 W / 280 m / 723 m. Both pieces under your 500m PB pace: 1:39.0 for 88 seconds, then 1:38.2 for 55, against a 1:39.9 PB.

Saturday's 7-stroke test peaked 580 W at drag 135. Today: 577 W at drag 127 — and then you kept rowing for another 80 seconds. Same ceiling, eight points less load per stroke, vastly more work after it. That is the better of the two efforts, not the lesser one.

Peak 577 → 88-second average 360 W is 62% of peak. Interval 2 averaged 369 W, 64%. Your ceiling is not the limiter — you reach ~580 W whether it takes seven strokes or one stroke — so the number that moves this score is how slowly it decays, which is exactly the anaerobic capacity your coaching profile already flagged.

You touched r49 building to peak, then settled to r38 and r40. Power rose 2.7% from piece one to piece two and all of it was turnover: work per stroke fell 568 → 554 J and length 7.97 → 7.64 m. Same signature as the 8×750 on Sep 11.
Two 20-second primers preceded it, nine and eighteen minutes out: 98m at r36 (≈329 W) then 105m at r42 (≈405 W). A 23% jump between them — you warm into power the way you warm into squats.
2026-09-14.watch: The decay, not the peak. 62% of peak held across 88 seconds is the benchmark to beat when this series comes round again — chasing a bigger Score A is chasing a number you already own.
2026-09-14.next: The last primer finished nine minutes before the clock started, and the two primers themselves were 23% apart. Interval 1 is the scored one, so it should be the effort you are most ready for; right now it is the one you are least ready for. Next challenge: ramp longer, finish the last primer 3–4 minutes out, and set drag deliberately for the piece length as you did here.

2026-09-16.title: Rowfit — VO₂ 10×1:30
2026-09-16.headline: You held the stroke this time. Same pace, 12.5% more work, a third of the length loss.
points: 3,842 m in 15:00 of work at 1:57.1 /500m, r30, 218 W. Band 1:54.9–2:04.9 — in zone, 2.8 s/500m quicker than the 1:59.9 midpoint. Hand-entered from the PM5: the erg never synced, so this one carries no logbook link.

Last week's brief was “finish the last rep still at 30–31 spm and ~8.4 m/stroke.” Last rep: r31, 8.47 m/stroke, 1:54.2, 235 W — the biggest stroke of the day AND the fastest split. You hit that to the decimal.

The fix landed exactly where it was flagged. Sep 9 halves: length 8.80 → 8.11 m (−7.8%), work per stroke −6.9%, rate +9.0% — and all of that bought 1.5% more power. Today: length 8.67 → 8.44 (−2.6%), work per stroke FLAT at +0.2%, rate +4.1% — and power rose 4.4%. Three times the negative split for a third of the cost.

Stroke economy sat on your line all the way: residual −0.25 spm in the first half, +0.25 in the second, 0.00 across the session. Sep 9 drifted −0.78 → +1.58, meaning by the end you were spending an extra 1.6 strokes a minute for that power. No drift at all today.
Against Sep 9 at the same rate (r30.3 → r30.0): 217 → 218 W, 430 → 437 J/stroke, 8.46 → 8.55 m/stroke — across 431 m and 1:40 more work. Every axis moved the right way at once.

Heart rate, now from the full FITIV export aligned to the piece: work-window means climbed 130 → 144 → 146 → 148 → 150 → 151 → 153 → 156 → 158 → 159, and peaks 153 → 169. Every rep higher than the last, and the rest floors climbed with them, 110 → 142. 196.5 kJ of work for 87.6 J per working heartbeat.

It never plateaued — rep 10 was still the highest of the day and still rising. That is the signature of a set that ended before your cardiovascular system did, not one that topped out: 47% of the piece in zone 4, nothing in zone 5, and 78 seconds total at or above the 167 threshold. Upper-threshold work, not VO₂max, and the structure is why.

Rep 1 was a second warm-up, not a rep. You came into it at 95 bpm after roughly three and a half minutes of near-rest between the warm-up and the first stroke, so it averaged 130 against rep 2's 144 — and it was also your slowest split, 1:58.1. Same shape as the squats: your first effort is always your worst. Closing that gap, or taking one primer piece 60–90 seconds before the clock starts, converts rep 1 from a throwaway into a tenth rep.

One thing off-prescription: the rate band was 30–34 and you ran 28–31, with three reps under the floor. The pace landed in zone anyway, which means you made it with a longer stroke than prescribed. Right direction for what you are chasing — just not what the card asked for.
2026-09-16.watch: I was wrong about the 52. FITIV's one-minute HR recovery card read 52 and I called it double-Elite; the exported series does not support it. Measured off your own data it is 21 bpm in the 60 s after your peak of 169, and 24 bpm in the 60 s after the last stroke — "Fit" on that same scale, not "Elite". Good, not extraordinary. Whatever FITIV is computing there, it is not a one-minute drop from peak.
2026-09-16.next: You have proved you can hold the stroke for 90 seconds. Now extend it — the same discipline at 2:00+ reps, which is where length normally goes first, and where heart rate finally gets time to sit at the top instead of spiking.
2026-09-16.diff: Sep 23 is VO₂ 8×500m, not 10×1:30: reps run about 2:00 instead of 1:30, a third longer under load, and the band tightens to 1:59.9–2:04.9 (75–80%), midpoint 2:02.4. Today's 1:57.1 is 2.8 s/500m quicker than the fast end of that — do not carry today's split across. Take the band and spend the difference on holding 8.4+ m/stroke to the last rep.

2026-09-18.title: Rowfit — Threshold 7×4min
2026-09-18.headline: Flattest set in the log — and I am the reason it was five seconds a rep too fast.
points: 6,746 m in 28:00 of work at 2:04.5 /500m, r27, 181 W, drag 116. Reps 1–6 came in at 960, 960, 963, 960, 961, 962 metres — a spread of 0.31%. Total pace range across all seven reps was 2.4 s/500m, and 2.0 s of that was rep 7 going faster. Nothing in your log is this flat.

The band was 2:09.9–2:14.9 (65–70%) and you rowed 2:04.5 — 75.4% of PB, 5.4 s/500m past the fast end and 7.9 s past the 2:12.4 midpoint. Before you ran it I told you “open at 2:03 and hold it,” which was wrong by about nine seconds a rep, and I corrected it afterwards. If you were working from the first number, this pace is on me, not on you.

Rep 7 is the one to look at: +5.7% power over the average of reps 1–6, and the split was stroke +5.0%, rate +0.6%. You finished by pulling harder, not by turning over faster. Sep 16's last rep was stroke +3.5% / rate +6.9%; today it is +5.0% / +0.6%. Three sessions running with a fast last rep, and the stroke's share of it has gone from none to most.

8.97 m per stroke, your longest of the week, at 26–27 s/m against a 26–28 prescription — bottom of the rate band again, holding pace with length instead of turnover. Economy residual −0.28 spm: sitting on your own line, with reps 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 inside ±0.06 of it.

Second threshold session in a row above band — Sep 11's 8×750 ran 77.8%. On a polarized week, Friday is the volume day that pays for Monday's sprints and Wednesday's VO₂. Run at 75% it stops being that and becomes a third hard day, three weeks out from Oct 10.
2026-09-18.watch: Which number you are pacing off. The card carries the band; I gave you a contradictory one and you rowed closer to mine. From here, trust the band on the card — for a 65–70% day that is 2:09.9–2:14.9, midpoint 2:12.4, and it should feel conversational and slightly boring. If a threshold day leaves you satisfied rather than under-worked, it was probably too fast.
2026-09-18.next: Row the band. The discipline you just showed holding six reps inside 3 metres is exactly what is needed at 2:12 — it is a harder skill at the slower pace, not an easier one, because there is nothing to hide behind.
2026-09-18.diff: Sep 25 is Threshold 2×15min, not 7×4min — two long grinders instead of seven short ones, and the band widens to 2:04.9–2:17.9 (62–75%), midpoint 2:11.4. Today's 2:04.5 sits right at the FAST end of that, so the pace you just held is legal there — but over 15 minutes rather than 4, which is a different proposition entirely. Start at the midpoint and earn your way down.
